en.title: United Boeing 757 lands safely at San Francisco after low-fuel go-around
en.summary: United flight UA1023 from Boston aborted its first landing attempt at San Francisco after an unstable approach, reported low fuel, and landed safely on its second attempt about 14 minutes later, with no injuries reported.
body: United Airlines flight UA1023, a Boeing 757-200 registered N19117, was operating from Boston Logan International Airport (BOS) to San Francisco International Airport (SFO) on the morning of Friday, October 30, when it aborted its landing on Runway 28R. Air traffic control had cleared the aircraft to land and warned the crew about wake turbulence from a Boeing 787 Dreamliner that had landed ahead of it, as well as a slight tailwind of five knots. ADS-B data showed the aircraft starting to climb at around 75 feet as the pilot initiated a go-around because of an unstable approach.

After the go-around, the crew climbed to 5,000 feet and reported 5,200 lbs of fuel remaining. The aircraft was cleared to land on Runway 28R a second time and touched down safely at 11:24 a.m. local time, about 14 minutes after the go-around. The flight carried 91 passengers and six crew members, and no injuries were reported.

Under U.S. rules for domestic flights, airlines must carry enough fuel to reach their destination and an alternate airport where required, plus a further 45 minutes of flying. The report notes that 5,200 lbs is close to the minimum threshold for a Boeing 757-200, although it is up to the pilots to decide whether to declare an emergency.

zh.title: 聯合航空波音757-200舊金山重飛後低油量安全降落無人受傷
zh.summary: 聯合航空1023號班機由波士頓飛往舊金山，10月30日上午因進場不穩定重飛，通報低油量後約14分鐘二度進場安全降落，無人受傷。
body: 聯合航空1023號班機為波音757-200型飛機，登記編號N19117，10月30日上午由波士頓洛根國際機場（BOS）飛往舊金山國際機場，在28R跑道首次進場時重飛。航管曾許可飛機降落，並提醒機組注意前方已降落的波音787夢幻客機尾流，以及約5節的順風。飛航追蹤資料顯示，飛機在約75英尺高度開始爬升，機組因進場不穩定而重飛。
重飛後，機組爬升至5000英尺，並通報剩餘燃油5200磅。飛機獲准二度進場28R跑道，於當地時間11時24分安全降落，距重飛約14分鐘。機上共有91名乘客與6名機組人員，無人受傷。
依美國國內航班規定，航空公司須攜帶足夠飛抵目的地與備降機場（如有需要）的燃油，另加45分鐘飛行所需燃油。報導指出，5200磅接近波音757-200的最低門檻，是否宣布緊急狀況由機組判斷。

After the go-around the crew climbed to 5,000 feet and reported 5,200 lbs of fuel remaining.
The aircraft landed safely on its second attempt at 11:24 a.m., about 14 minutes after the go-around, with 91 passengers and six crew aboard and no injuries reported.
U.S. domestic flights must carry enough fuel to reach their destination and an alternate where required, plus a further 45 minutes of flying.
